newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville to offer firm, non-firm peak power Tues.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville to offer firm, non-firm peak power Tues.

text.p: Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) will again offer peak load power Tuesday for both firm and non-firm delivery after only offering non-firm, peak power Friday, the federal agency said Monday.
BPA offered firm, peak Tuesday electricity at $24.75 a megawatt hour (MWh) for all deliveries, $25.25 in the Northwest and $26.00 at the California-Oregon Border (COB) and Nevada-Oregon Border (NOB).
There is a 300 megawatt (MW) volume limit for firm, peak power.
Tuesday BPA power for non-firm delivery was offered at $17.75/MWh for the hours ending 0600 and 2300 PST.
Same-term electricity in COB, NOB and Northwest was offered at $18.50, down from Friday's $20.00 for COB and $22.00 for Northwest.
BPA non-firm power between 1100-1600 PST Tuesday was offered at $23.25 for all deliveries, $24.00 for the Northwest and $25.00 at COB and NOB.
BPA placed a 500 MW purchase limit on the five-hour blocks of power.
